liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Deal** (4 reviews): Reviewer says most fans consider this the best Deal the band ever played; Deal rocks, though reviewer says an Alpine version might be slightly better [17][18][19][25]
- **Ramble on Rose** (2 reviews): The crowd chanted for Phil at the end of the song, before Box of Rain; The crowd's repeated chant for Phil sounded like a single voice [16][26]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (2 reviews): Once Weir got past the amp static, the show began to cook around this song; Reviewer calls this Minglewood very hot, with nasty fills from Brent [24][25]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer loves this Morning Dew and calls Garcia's playing brilliant [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-06-21.142379.schoeps.cmc4.mk2s.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 192 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd89-06-21.sbd.gorinsky.4603.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 192 min; rated 3.93/5 by 15 [3]
- **gd1989-06-21.151620.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 189 min [4]
- **gd1989-06-21.144779.mtx.tobin.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 197 min [6]
- **gd1989-06-21.175537.5-1.fix.tobin.flac1648**: source not stated; 23 songs; 197 min [9]
- **gd89-06-21.satellite-uplink.nawrocki.16888.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 196 min; rated 3.86/5 by 7 [14]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the sound is very good and Jerry's voice is solid [24]

## Around the show

- Weir's amplifier caught fire early on; the band jammed while the crew replaced it [15]
- Clarence Clemons played saxophone during the second set [15]
- Reviewer found the saxophone playing poor, though the rest of the show is solid [19]
- The band had equipment problems at the start of the show [23]
- The pay-per-view broadcast ended before the concert did [23]
- Equipment troubles made a haggard beginning for a show sold to huge pay-per-view audiences [24]
- Clarence Clemons sat in from Ship of Fools through Turn On Your Lovelight [1]
- The show was a pay-per-view video broadcast and a national FM broadcast [1]
- Reviewer found no memorable renditions and called it a fairly standard late-1980s Dead show [15]
- Reviewer ranks it among the best of 1989, strong despite the band's usual weakness on TV broadcasts and festivals [17]
- Band plays certain numbers as rocking set pieces rather than smoothly transitional jamming [18]
- Reviewer considers it a solid representation of Summer '89 [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-06-21.142379.schoeps.cmc4.mk2s.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience Dat; Schoeps CMC4/MK2S mics spaced on 2 stands, OTS > Panasonic SV-250 (16-bit/48k); Transfer Info:… [1]
- **gd89-06-21.sbd.gorinsky.4603.sbeok.shnf**: source: Digital PPV feed> Master VHS> Dan Sisler's 1st-gen professionally dubbed VHS> DAT transfer by Sisler (Sony PCM R-500 via SBM)> CDR transfer by Kevin Gills on… [3]. Also: Reviewer got a copy from the national radio broadcast, thought to be Westwood One, hence the clean sound [16]
- **gd1989-06-21.151620.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  November 7, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [4]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters make it complete; the mix differs from the pay-per-view [4]
- **gd1989-06-21.144779.mtx.tobin.flac1644**: transferred by Mixed by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) [6]. Also: A mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in January 2018 [6]
- **gd1989-06-21.175537.5-1.fix.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound Mix (48k) by Kevin Tobin; source: 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound Mix (48k) [9]. Also: A mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in December 2025 [9]
- **gd89-06-21.satellite-uplink.nawrocki.16888.sbeok.shnf**: source: Satellite uplink > Houston Tracker 8+ C-Band Satellite receiver w/ Video Cipher II digital descrambler (on Galaxy 3, Transponder 21) > JVC HR-S8000U Super VHS… [14]
